plan.contextChunk: This figure contains three panels that together build a complete mechanistic picture of how the reversible reaction N2O4(g) ⇌ 2NO2(g) approaches chemical equilibrium. Panel (a) shows molecular-scale snapshots of a sealed container at t = 0, pre-equilibrium, and at equilibrium: starting from only large, colorless N2O4 molecules, the mixture progressively gains smaller brown NO2 molecules until a stable proportion of both coexists, mirrored by the color change from colorless to deep orange-brown in the tube icons above. Panel (b) plots concentration versus time, with [N2O4] falling and [NO2] rising along smooth curves that both plateau once the shaded Equilibrium achieved region is entered. Panel (c) plots reaction rates versus time, showing the forward rate k_f[N2O4] decreasing and the reverse rate k_r[NO2]^2 increasing until the two curves merge at a common constant value. Together the three panels demonstrate that equilibrium is a dynamic state defined by equal opposing rates rather than a cessation of reaction, motivating the quantitative equilibrium constant that follows.

interactionPlan.concept: Chemical equilibrium in the reversible reaction N2O4 ⇌ 2NO2 is a dynamic state reached when the forward and reverse reaction rates become equal, producing constant (but generally unequal) concentrations of both species.
elements: panel (a): three sealed-container vials labeled 't = 0', 'pre-equilibrium', 'at equilibrium', each showing a molecular mix of N2O4 molecules (two blue N atoms each bonded to two red O atoms) and NO2 molecules (one blue N with two red O)
panel (a): color tube icons above each vial fading from colorless (t = 0) through pale yellow to deep orange-brown (equilibrium), with curved arrows pointing into each vial
panel (a): labels 'N2O4' and 'NO2' identifying the two molecule types

panel (b): concentration vs time graph with x-axis 'Time' (origin 0) and y-axis 'Concentration', falling blue curve labeled N2O4, rising brown/orange curve labeled NO2, vertical dashed line and shaded region labeled 'Equilibrium achieved'

panel (c): rate vs time graph with x-axis 'Time' and y-axis 'Rate', falling blue curve labeled k_f[N2O4], rising brown/orange curve labeled k_r[NO2]^2, curves merging at a shared plateau, dashed line and shaded 'Equilibrium achieved' region
movable vertical time marker line spanning the active graph, with readout of current concentrations or rates

interactions.label: Time marker
interactions.teaches: At any instant the vial color, molecular populations, concentrations, and opposing rates all correspond — dragging through time shows N2O4 being consumed and NO2 accumulating until both level off together at equilibrium

interactions.label: Initial N2O4 concentration
interactions.teaches: Changing the starting amount of N2O4 shifts where the concentration curves plateau and the common equilibrium rate, while the same qualitative approach to equal rates always occurs — the equilibrium position depends on initial conditions, the dynamic nature does not

interactions.label: Graph quantity
interactions.teaches: The same time course can be viewed as concentrations becoming constant or as forward and reverse rates becoming equal — the plateau in one view is the curve-merging in the other

demo_steps.title: Watch the approach
demo_steps.narration: Drag the time marker from t = 0: the vial darkens from colorless toward orange-brown as N2O4 falls and NO2 rises on the concentration graph. The curves are still changing — the system is not yet at equilibrium.

demo_steps.title: Equilibrium achieved
demo_steps.narration: Move the marker into the shaded region: concentrations stop changing and the vial color stabilizes, even though both molecule types are still present and reacting.

demo_steps.title: The rate view
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the rate graph: at equilibrium the forward rate k_f[N2O4] and reverse rate k_r[NO2]^2 have merged — the reaction has not stopped, the two opposing processes exactly balance.

demo_steps.title: Change the starting conditions
demo_steps.narration: Adjust the initial N2O4 concentration: the plateau levels, equilibrium color, and merged rate value all shift together, showing equilibrium position depends on where you start.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Equilibrium is dynamic, not static: the concentrations stop changing because the forward and reverse reaction rates have become equal, not because the reactions have ceased.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Three-part vertical layout matching the source: molecular panel (a) on top, single graph panel below that toggles between concentration (b) and rate (c) views. Panel (a) shows three round-bottom vials side by side; inside, N2O4 drawn as a blue-blue pair each with two red oxygens (larger), NO2 as a single blue with two reds (smaller). t=0 vial holds only N2O4 (~6 molecules), pre-equilibrium a mix with NO2 appearing, equilibrium a stable mix leaning toward NO2. Tube icons above vials shift from pale grey-blue to yellow to orange-brown, and should cross-fade smoothly as the time marker moves rather than snapping between three discrete states. Graph panel: axes unscaled (no numeric ticks, just 0 at origin), blue curve always the N2O4-linked quantity falling, brown/orange curve the NO2-linked quantity rising, shaded pale-yellow region right of a dashed vertical line labeled 'Equilibrium achieved'. In Rate view the two curves merge into a single plateau line; in Concentration view they plateau at different heights with NO2 above N2O4. The time marker is a draggable vertical line on the graph synced to the vial display and color tube above.

authoredContext:
illustrates fundamental equilibrium concepts using the reversible decomposition of colorless dinitrogen tetroxide to yield brown nitrogen dioxide, an elementary reaction described by the equation:

As the reaction begins ( t = 0), the concentration of the N 2 O 4 reactant is finite and that of the NO 2 product is zero, so the forward reaction proceeds at a finite rate while the reverse reaction rate is zero. As time passes, N 2 O 4 is consumed and its concentration falls, while NO 2 is produced and its concentration increases ( b ). The decreasing concentration of the reactant slows the forward reaction rate, and the increasing product concentration speeds the reverse reaction rate ( c ). This process continues until the forward and reverse reaction rates become equal , at which time the reaction has reached equilibrium, as characterized by constant concentrations of its reactants and products (shaded areas of b and c ). It’s important to emphasize that chemical equilibria are dynamic; a reaction at equilibrium has not “stopped,” but is proceeding in the forward and reverse directions at the same rate. This dynamic nature is essential to understanding equilibrium behavior as discussed in this and subsequent chapters of the text.

Note that a special double arrow is used to emphasize the reversible nature of the reaction.

(a) A sealed tube containing colorless N 2 O 4 darkens as it decomposes to yield brown NO 2 . (b) Changes in concentration over time as the decomposition reaction achieves equilibrium. (c) At equilibrium, the forward and reverse reaction rates are equal.

A three-part diagram is shown and labeled, “a,” “b,” and “c.” In part a, at the top of the diagram, three beakers are shown, and each one contains a sealed tube. The tube in the left beaker is labeled “t equals 0.” It is full of a colorless gas which is connected to a zoom-in view of the particles in the tube by a downward-facing arrow. This particle view shows seven particles, each composed of two connected blue spheres. Each blue sphere is connected to two red spheres. This type of particle is labeled “N subscript 2 O subscript 4.” The tube in the middle beaker is labeled “pre-equilibrium.” It is full of a light brown gas which is connected to a zoom-in view of the particles in the tube by a downward-facing arrow. This particle view shows nine particles, five of which are composed of two connected blue spheres. Each blue sphere is connected to two red spheres. This type of particle is labeled “N subscript 2 O subscript 4.” The remaining four are composed of two red spheres connected to a blue sphere. This type of particle is labeled “N O subscript 2.”  The tube in the right beaker is labeled “at equilibrium.” It is full of a brown gas which is connected to a zoom-in view of the particles in the tube by a downward-facing arrow. This particle view shows eleven particles, three of which are composed of two connected blue spheres. Each blue sphere is connected to two red spheres. The remaining eight are composed of two red spheres connected to a blue sphere. In part b, in the middle of the image, is one graph. This graph has a y-axis labeled, “Concentration,” and an x-axis labeled, “Time.” A red line labeled, “N O subscript 2,” begins in the bottom left corner of the graph at a point labeled, “0,” and rises near the highest point on the y-axis before it levels off and becomes horizontal. A blue line labeled, “N subscript 2 O subscript 4,” begins near the highest point on the y-axis and drops below the midpoint of the y-axis before leveling off. In part c, at the bottom of the image is another graph. This graph has a y-axis labeled, “Rate,” and an x-axis labeled, “Time.” A red line labeled, “k subscript f, [ N subscript 2 O subscript 4 ],” begins in the bottom left corner of the graph at a point labeled, “0,” and rises near the middle of the y-axis before it levels off and becomes horizontal. A blue line labeled, “k subscript f, [ N O subscript 2 ] superscript 2,” begins near the highest point on the y-axis and drops to the same point on the y-axis as the red line before leveling off. The point where both lines become horizontal is labeled, “Equilibrium achieved.”

discrepancies: Source graph (b) has no vertical time-marker line or numeric readout; the generated figure adds a green marker line and text readout across the plot (pedagogically fine but not in the source)

The middle test tube's color in the source is a fixed pale yellow for 'pre-equilibrium', while the generated figure tints it dynamically (amber at the default t=15), making the default state darker than the source
The curved pouring arrows from tube to vial in the source are replaced by short curved ticks whose arrowhead points into the vial rim awkwardly, weakening the 'pouring in' reading
Curve labels in the source sit directly adjacent to their curves in black; the generated rate-view labels use literal underscores ('k_f[N₂O₄]') rather than subscript formatting
Source panels (b) and (c) are both visible simultaneously; the generated figure shows only one graph at a time behind a checkbox toggle
evaluation.notes: A faithful three-panel equilibrium figure: molecular vials with correct N₂O₄/NO₂ ball models and tube coloring, correct decay/rise concentration curves with shaded equilibrium region, plus a genuinely functional rate-view toggle, time slider, initial-concentration slider, and a 4-step guided demo that correctly teaches dynamic equilibrium; only minor styling deviations (added time marker, underscore-formatted rate labels, tube tint) separate it from the source.
action_items: Render the rate labels with true subscripts (e.g. tspan baseline-shift for 'f' and 'r') instead of literal 'k_f' / 'k_r' underscores
Soften or shorten the added green time-marker line, or start the demo with the marker hidden/at t=0, so the default state matches the clean source graph (b)
Redraw the tube-to-vial arrows as the source's clear curved arrows with the arrowhead entering the vial opening

feedback.rationale: Scores are high (4-5 across all dimensions), the concept and interactivity are fully correct, and the remaining discrepancies are minor styling deviations that don't impair understanding — further iteration offers little gain.
